newsitem.title: CHINA: China Res, CKI up after joining blue chips.
newsitem.headline: China Res, CKI up after joining blue chips.

text.p: Shares of China Resources Enterprise Ltd and Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) tended higher in line with the market after they joined the blue-chip Hang Seng Index on Thursday.

"The impact on the firms from joining the blue-chip index was already reflected in the recent rallies in their share prices," said Sunny Chan, research manager at Seapower Securities. "Today's surge was following the overall market."
CKI shares hit a morning high of HK$27.20 before they steadied at HK$26.90 in mid-morning, unchanged from their previous close. Volume was 1.32 million shares.
Shares of China Resources rose HK$0.70 to HK$38.70 on volume of 2.78 million shares.
"Recent strong sentiment on red-chip stocks also aided demand for China Resources," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
Brokers said speculation of asset injection among China parent-backed firms continued to beef up demand for red-chips.
But they expected profit-taking to cap the upside of the stocks in the near run.
